evidence: STRUCTURE (source reading, supports a graded reward). tests/scoring.toml weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05, gates 0.0; tests/tools/score.py computes reward = round(weighted mean, 4) once gates and floor pass, so the reward is continuous. Functional: 152 binary criteria, aggregation weighted_mean, total weight 64.4042; smallest 0.01, largest 2.5 (3.9% of the dimension), so no single criterion dominates. My grouping by criterion id: 98 underlying offer-desk rows (P1-P10) = 31.1% of functional, 44 hro_change_* rows = 44.9%, 10 desk/live/entries/keep rows = 24.1%. Polish: 5 binary rows weighted 3/2.5/1.5/2/3. Visual: 5 likert rows (points 5, five anchors each, weight 1.2). tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:15 tells the judge to 'score EACH criterion independently, continue after failure' and that 'Shared scenarios ... are not conjunctive scoring bundles'; most rows carry their own fallback ('use an independent ordinary successful ...', 'If P4 cannot advance ...'), so one failed chain is not meant to zero its siblings. Hand-derived tiers from the weights (NOT measured): (a) offer desk only, no coordinated-change desk -> functional at most 0.311, polish 0, visual by craft: reward about 0.19 plus up to 0.20 visual; (b) plus saved previews and commit but no pre-save figures, live updates or kept entries -> functional up to about 0.76; (c) full desk -> up to 1.0. Partial apps therefore land at distinct intermediate rewards by design. PRECONDITIONS. The in-dimension gate in all three scored prompts is one requisition create plus fresh-context readback, the same bar as the constraints gate, so it adds no new cliff. By my reading 32 of the 44 hro_change_* rows (37.3% of functional) need a coordinated commit that succeeds, and all five polish rows need the Coordinated Changes editor (polish/judge.toml: saved preview, editor entries, preview save, commit refusal, lost commit response). That is the headline feature of instruction.md:1-3, so I treat it as a concentration, not a defect. FLOOR. A create-only app that passes both gates but computes no figures scores about 0.03 functional by my estimate, below the 0.05 floor, so reward is 0 and visual credit is discarded. That is the template policy (scoring.toml is byte-identical to the template) and belongs to check 43. RUNTIME (missing). raw-evidence-index.json scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and target/Oracle scores are absent.' Its 10 artifacts are scripted golden observations; all 10 sha256 values match the files on disk. The run directory holds no reward-discrimination or reward-ordering record, which qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:31 requires before local clearance. No weak or mutated app has been graded by the configured judge, so no spread has been observed. HARNESS CLIFF (unmeasured). tests/test.sh:224-226 'if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0' leaves the pre-written zero reward when rewardkit exits non-zero or hits the 11100 s suite budget (test.sh is identical to the template). The functional judge runs 152 criteria and the P1-P10, B1-B6, D, L, E, R protocols in one batched session with timeout 9000 (functional/judge.toml:4). No configured judge duration exists. If that session overruns, every submission scores 0 regardless of quality, which would make the reward all-or-nothing in practice. I could not determine from the files read how rewardkit reports a judge timeout. Row-level budget exhaustion is handled more gently: the prompts return 0 with 'NOT EXERCISED' for unobserved rows, which compresses the spread toward the bottom rather than collapsing it.
counterexample: Not demonstrated; two plausible cases. Broken app that could score like a better one: none found from the weights. Conforming app that could score 0: a complete, correct desk whose functional judge session exceeds 9000 s (or whose scored suite exceeds 11100 s) keeps the zero written at the start of test.sh, the same reward as a blank app. Whether this happens is unknown because no configured judge run has been timed.
suggested_fix: Obtain the two required hash-bound runtime records: grade the golden and at least two mutated weak apps (for example commit disabled; live updates disabled) with the configured judge, and record the functional judge duration against the 9000 s timeout. Change no budget or weight without that measurement and explicit authorization.
